newsitem.title: CROATIA: Mixed Croatia stocks seen picking up activity.
newsitem.headline: Mixed Croatia stocks seen picking up activity.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed in Wednesday's modest trade, but market participants foresaw trading volume swelling in the following weeks, bolstering prices.
"I foresee mild gains for (blue chips) Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka and all the other prices to follow in their footsteps," Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage told Reuters.
"Prices are likely to fluctuate within a 5-6 percent range," he added.

Traders predicted further steady growth of fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka, based on its outstanding 1996 business results released last week, which started a new wave of investment in Croatia's small share market.
Zagrebacka was the day's most active stock, inching up 0.20 kuna to 2,000.20 with 3,415 units changing hands.
Another blue chip, Pliva pharmaceuticals was also among the gainers. It added five kuna to 480 on volume of 1,571 units.
Four of 15 active issues rose on Wednesday, five fell and six were unchanged. Volume dipped to 9,596 shares from over 30,000, and turnover was halved at 10 million kuna.
Hotelier Arenaturist which rose nine kuna to 149 led the gainers selling 220 shares. The most active hotelier was Suncani Hvar which edged down one kuna to 63 on volume of 1,140 shares.
But Kos singled out Laguna as one of the best buys among hoteliers.
"If we take a better look, Laguna is, in the long run, probably the most stable stock of all," he said. It rose 30 kuna to 1,500 on volume of 506 units.
Food procesor Podravka, flat at 308 kuna, was among the most active stocks with 1,711 shares changing hands.
Chocolate maker Kras registered marginal losses, inching down one kuna to 460 kuna on volume of 125.
Varazdinska Banka first issue ordinary share, included last week in the Zagreb bourse's first quotation, led the day's losers. It dipped eight percent or 4,000 kuna to 45,000 with only 16 units sold.
